title: Manchester United: Rooney's dark confession lands as the results slide
body:
Wayne Rooney has disclosed that there was a stretch of his Manchester United career when he thought about ending his own life [S1]. He has also said he sought help from a therapist to work out what was going on inside him [S2].

Sky Sports tied the admission to the lowest point of his time at the club [S1]. BBC Sport carried the same central claim, reporting that the thoughts came while he was still playing there [S2]. The story is heavy, and it deserves to be treated as a human one first.

Now look at the football. Across their last five league matches, the side have won none, drawn three and lost two, collecting just three points [ST1]. They have scored six and conceded eleven [ST1]. That is a team leaking goals and struggling to build any momentum, which is a grim backdrop for anyone already carrying something heavy.

The lesson here is that a famous shirt can be a crushing weight, and that the noise around results should never drown out the person wearing it. Fans love to judge players by their scorelines, but this story shows how little those numbers reveal about what is happening behind the scenes.

The Touchline Take: one to keep an eye on, because the person behind the headline matters more than the table.
